Surah 82: Al-Infitar (The Cleaving)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾: split open.
﴿And when the stars fall, scattered﴾, they drop down.

And when the seas are made to overflow (fujjirat) (Qur'an 82:3). [Translation of the tafsir passage follows.]

Opened up, one into another, and the seas became a single sea.

And when the graves are overturned (بُعْثِرَتْ),

﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾: they are excavated, and their dead are brought out. And the answer (jawab) of "idha" (إذا, "when") is:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 82, verse 5:

.

﴿A soul will know﴾, i.e., every soul, righteous and wicked,

﴿what it has sent forward﴾, what it has done of obedience,

﴿and what it has left behind﴾, and abandoned, so that it did not act; or: what it sent forward of charities, and what it left behind of inheritance.

O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous, who created you, fashioned you, and made you proportionate?

It is said: the address is to those who deny the Resurrection.

﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ﴾ "O man" (al-insan). It is said that the address is to those who deny the resurrection (al-ba'th).

﴿ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الكَرِيمِ﴾ ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ﴾ What deceived you, such that you neglected what was incumbent upon you, despite the generosity of your Lord, in that He bestowed upon you blessings of creation, proportioning (tasdiyah), and balancing (ta'dil)? And from Him ﷺ, when he recited it: "Ignorance of it deceived him." And from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "His foolishness deceived him." And from al-Hasan: "His Satan deceived him." And from al-Fudayl: "If I were addressed, I would say: 'Your veils let down deceived me.'" And from Yahya ibn Mu'adh: "I would say: 'Your kindness to me, past and present, deceived me.'"

﴿فَسَوّاكَ﴾ So He made you (fa-sawwaka), i.e., made you of balanced form (mustawi al-khalq), with all your limbs sound. "Fa-'addalaka" (then He balanced you): He made you moderate and proportionate in form, without any disparity in it, so that He did not make one hand longer, nor one eye wider, nor some limbs white and others black. Or it means He made you of balanced form, walking upright, unlike the beasts. The reading with lightening (takhfif), "Kufi," has the same meaning as the intensified form, namely: He equalized some of your limbs with others until they were balanced, so you were of balanced creation and proportionate.

"In whatever form He willed, He assembled you."

"ما" is extra (zā'idah), for emphasis. That is: He assembled you in whatever form His will required, from the various forms that differ in beauty and ugliness, tallness and shortness. This clause was not joined with a conjunction as the preceding clause was, because it is an explanation (bayān) of "ʿadalaka" (He proportioned you). The prepositional phrase (al-jārr wa-al-majrūr) is connected to "rakkabaka" (He assembled you), in the sense of: He placed you in some forms and empowered you within them; or it is connected to an omitted verb, meaning: He assembled you as existing in some of the forms.

"Kalla" (ﷻ no; "kalla" is a particle of reproof) — translating now.

Kallā: a rebuke against heedlessness of Allah (Exalted),

Bal tukadhdhibūna bil-dīn: rather, you deny the Religion (dīn) at its root, and it is the recompense (al-jazā'), or the religion of Islam. So you do not believe in reward or punishment.
﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾, [guarding] your deeds and your words, from among the angels.

Translation:

﴿Noble scribes﴾, meaning: indeed you deny the recompense, and the scribes are writing down your deeds for you, so that you may be repaid for them.

(Verse 12:) ﴿They know what you do.﴾ Nothing of your deeds is hidden from them. Praising the scribes (al-kataba) and commending them serves to magnify the matter of recompense, and shows that it is among the great affairs in the sight of God. It also contains a warning and a terrifying threat to the guilty, and a kindness (lutf) to the God-fearing. It is related from al-Fudayl that when he recited it he said: "How severe a verse it is for the heedless!"
Qur'an 82:13: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will surely be in bliss.﴾ Indeed, the believers will surely be in the bliss of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 82, verse 14:

﴿Indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾, and indeed, the disbelievers will be in the Fire.

Translation:

﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Judgment﴾: they will enter it on the Day of Recompense.

(p-612) ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾, meaning: they will not come out of it, like His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And they will never leave it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 37]. Then He magnified the matter of the Day of Resurrection, saying:

﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?﴾ ﴿Then, what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?﴾ He repeated it for emphasis and to convey the magnitude of the matter, and he clarified it with His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 82, verse 19:

﴿The Day when no soul will have power at all for another soul﴾ meaning: it will not be able to repel anything from it, nor bring it any benefit in any way; intercession will only be possessed by permission. "Yawmu" (the Day), with a nominative ending (raf'), is the reading of Makki and Basri, meaning: "it is the Day of..." or it is in apposition to "yawm al-din" (the Day of Judgement). Whoever reads it in the accusative (nasb) does so by supposing an implied "udhkur" (remember), or an implied "yudanun" (they will be recompensed), because "al-din" (the Judgement/recompense) points to it.

﴿And the command on that Day belongs to Allah﴾ meaning: there is no command except that of Allah (Exalted) alone; He is the one who judges in it, to the exclusion of any other.
